markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

Three starting-point insights guide this early-stage proposal. Padding errors of 1.5769–1.9719 exceed the 1e-5 tolerance, confounding context-removal interpretation. Movies and Electronics have sampled negative-win rates of 6.25% and 5.90%; these motivate discrimination experiments without establishing validation weakness. Users report stale-interest emphasis and broad alternatives displacing precise matches, motivating separate temporal and ranking hypotheses.

Three related-work insights refine implementation. Packed GRUs require chronological compaction before packing [1]. BPR-max aggregates pairwise probabilities, with gradients through negative softmax weights and a separate score penalty [2,3]. Timestamp decay differs from event-distance weighting; normalization must account for actual target exposure to avoid unintended changes in user contribution.

### Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Atomic proposal | O/F/U/M/D scores |
|---|---|---|
| Encoding correctness | Compact, pack, and scatter GRU outputs | 2/8/5/10/4 |
| Ranking discrimination | BPR-max with 16 uniform negatives | 3/7/7/8/4 |
| Target relevance | Normalized user-relative timestamp weights | 4/6/8/5/5 |

Scores denote originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, and difficulty. For encoding, respective positives are focused adaptation, reusable correctness, stable histories, direct padding repair, and standard APIs; negatives are established machinery, uncertain accuracy gains, indirect user benefits, unresolved margins, and alignment bookkeeping. For BPR-max: positives are controlled adaptation, reusable objectives, competitive discrimination, weak-margin targeting, and compact implementation; negatives are established methodology, dataset dependence, false negatives, training-only evidence, and sampling cost. For recency: positives are explicit exposure control, temporal relevance, current-interest emphasis, testable supervision, and simple decay; negatives are incremental novelty, durable-interest suppression, unproven user benefit, confounded existing evidence, and normalization complexity.

### Selected experiment

Select **padding-invariant GRU4Rec with separately tested BPR-max and normalized user-relative recency weighting**. At 20% progress, retain this feasible direction; defer temporal gates and text features. It targets stale interests displacing recent behavior and broad alternatives displacing closer matches, while directly repairing measured padding failure. Compatibility and satisfied needs remain unresolved.

```
compact chronological real inputs; pack nonempty rows
run supplied GRU; unpack and scatter aligned features
sample 16 distinct eligible uniform negatives
loss_t = -logsumexp(log_softmax(s_neg)+logsigmoid(s_pos-s_neg))
a_t = 0.5 + 0.5*exp(-(latest_train_time-target_time)/tau)
Z_u = expectation_of_a_under_actual_target_exposure(u)
optimize baseline_reduction((a_t/Z_u)*loss_t)
```

First verify padding equivalence, then compare the corrected baseline objective against BPR-max with identical example and negative draws; enable recency last. Keep linear scores and zero score penalty initially. Estimate all temporal quantities from training histories; retain uniform weights when exposure normalization cannot be established. Keep window-position weighting separate.

Preserve four-category routing, seeds, limits, diagnostic interfaces, matching predictor code, and exactly one checkpoint per category. Use pinned macro validation HR@10 alone for selection. Log weighted user mass and effective sample size; cap comparisons to limit validation overfitting. No proposed improvement has been measured.

idea.description: Make the supplied GRU4Rec encoding invariant to left padding, then independently test BPR-max and bounded, exposure-normalized user-relative timestamp weighting. Retain exactly one independently trained GRU model per category. Treat encoding repair as a prerequisite and the two learning changes as separate hypotheses.
idea.motivation: All four supplied padding diagnostics fail, so encoding correctness precedes interpreting recency interventions. Competitive-negative training targets broad alternatives crowding out precise matches; timestamp weighting targets older or occasional interests displacing recent behavior. These explicitly address two reported user-facing failure modes, but neither guarantees precise compatibility, complementary usefulness, or avoidance of already-satisfied needs. The measured model-facing target is padding inconsistency, followed by weak sampled margins in Movies_and_TV and Electronics. Training diagnostics do not establish validation improvement.
idea.implementation_notes:
Encoding: preserve the supplied GRU backbone, embedding and output transformations. Compact each row's nonzero tokens chronologically into right-padded storage; pack only nonempty rows with CPU lengths, batch_first=True and enforce_sorted=False. Never pack the original left-padded array. Unpack with total_length=L and scatter valid outputs to the original nonpadding indices; for strictly left-padded histories these are L-length+j. Automatic packing restores batch order, so do not unsort again. Apply existing output projections consistently to valid states and explicitly zero padding features afterward. Empty histories receive documented zero features without executing a synthetic recurrent step. Use the maximum nonpadding index for final readout, never count-1. The top-layer h_n[-1] is the final recurrent state; any existing projection must also be applied before treating it as the scoring feature.

Compatibility: preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence) returning aligned B x L features, predict_score(features, items), family-specific sample_batch, ModelView, and the actual trained nn.Module at view.model. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), using measured metrics and their definitions. Keep the diagnostic loader's (None, sequence, positive, negative) tuple unchanged. Obtain training-only timestamp and original target-index information through a separate sampler side channel. Training, diagnostics and the embedded predictor writer must use identical encoding and score transformations.

Loss: use raw linear scores in the initial comparison; if the supplied baseline uses another activation, hold that activation fixed for the first objective comparison and document it. For each valid training position, sample 16 distinct uniform negatives excluding zero, the target and observed training positives. Use all eligible items if fewer than 16 exist, mask unused slots before softmax, and skip positions with no eligible negatives using the same validity mask in both objectives. This filtered, without-replacement sampler intentionally differs from official GRU4Rec's shared, with-replacement pools and limited collision masking. Implement BPR-max as -logsumexp(log_softmax(negative_scores) + logsigmoid(positive_score-negative_scores)); gradients flow through softmax weights. Do not divide BPR-max by the negative count or detach the weights. Initially set its separate negative-score penalty lambda to zero. A later penalty comparison uses lambda*sum(softmax(s_neg)*s_neg^2), distinct from optimizer weight decay. Preserve the baseline reduction and optimizer between objective comparisons; when extending a pairwise baseline to multiple negatives, explicitly use its mean across eligible negatives to avoid count-dependent scaling. Record that reduction as part of the control.

Temporal objective: define age(u,j)=latest_training_timestamp(u)-original_target_timestamp(u,j), using consistent timestamp units. Set a(u,j)=0.5+0.5*exp(-age/tau). Fix tau to the category median of strictly positive user training-history spans; if none exist, disable temporal weighting for that category. For missing or invalid user timestamps, use weights of one for the entire user rather than mixing valid and fabricated ages. Let q(j|u) be the actual baseline exposure distribution over eligible loss positions, including crop draws, truncation, repeated window inclusion and baseline per-window reduction. Compute Z_u=sum_j q(j|u)*a(u,j) and multiply that user's baseline position losses by a/Z_u. This preserves expected baseline user mass while redistributing supervision toward recent targets. Derive q from the supplied sampler's exact law or enumerate its finite window distribution; if it cannot be established, retain uniform weights and defer the temporal arm. Do not substitute biased batch self-normalization. If implementing an independently specified desired distribution p instead, use p/q only where q has nonzero support. Do not apply recency through both target sampling and loss weighting. Preserve the baseline user sampler; equal-user claims apply only if that sampler and reduction actually give equal user mass.

Controls: first compare the supplied encoding and padding-invariant encoding under the same baseline objective. Then compare the padding-corrected baseline objective against BPR-max using identical initialization, examples, negative-ID tensors, score activation, optimizer and update budget. Use a sampler RNG separate from model randomness, with seed 42, and replay draws or generate them deterministically from update indices. Enable normalized temporal weighting only after these comparisons. Keep negative-count and score-penalty changes separate; a later count comparison should use prefixes of one maximum-size negative pool with batch size fixed. Full-history event-distance weighting and sampled-window-position weighting are distinct optional controls; the latter can weight the same target differently across crops. Do not spend budget comparing normalized pure exponential global and user-relative decay when their user-specific multiplicative factor cancels exactly. That equivalence does not automatically hold for the proposed additive-floor decay. Optional training-only gap permutations can test gap placement beyond event order, but are exploratory and consume the same budget.

Verification and reporting: compare every valid timestep, final state and candidate score against individual unpadded executions in eval mode. Include unsorted and tied lengths, singleton and full histories, mixed and all-empty batches, batch permutations, added leading padding, and different batch companions. Check zero padding outputs and numerical agreement within the declared 1e-5 tolerance; investigate compaction, scattering and readout separately if it fails. Re-run the measured diagnostics only after equivalence passes. Log target inclusion frequency, baseline and weighted user contribution, and effective sample size (sum weights)^2/sum squared weights. History-length, activity-rate and history-end-date analyses are exploratory and must use training-derived strata with reported sample counts. Do not interpret feature sensitivity as useful recency, embedding alignment as diversity, or sampled margins as full-catalog ranking quality.

Protocol: preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution and the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, including failed trials and diagnostics. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; ratings, reviews, category metadata, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unavailable. No pretrained weights, additional datasets, hidden test access or other-trial checkpoints. Write working/predict.py through the predictor writer with matching architecture/configuration and exactly one selected checkpoint per category. Preserve native full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10 over 200 users/category and 99 unique negatives with evaluation seed 42. Prespecify the comparison order, checkpoint-selection schedule and maximum affordable trial count before execution; retain full validation records to expose selection overfitting. No model, checkpoint or score averaging is permitted. The actual supplied baseline code is absent from this report, so exact sampler normalization and integration must be verified against that code before implementation.
idea.pseudocode:
Set preprocessing_seed=0 and training_seed=42
Prespecify comparison order, validation schedule and trial budget
For each of the four required categories:
    Load supplied fixed splits through os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
    Initialize the supplied GRU4Rec using seed 42
    Encode(sequence):
        Allocate zero aligned features
        Select nonempty rows and collect original nonpadding indices
        Compact real tokens chronologically into right-padded storage
        Pack with CPU lengths and enforce_sorted=False
        Run the existing unidirectional GRU
        Unpack with total_length=L; retain restored input batch order
        Apply existing output transformations consistently
        Scatter valid features to original nonpadding indices
        Return aligned features, leaving padding and empty rows zero
    Verify valid features and scores against individual unpadded executions
    Read final features at maximum nonpadding index; handle empty rows explicitly
    If temporal arm is enabled:
        Derive actual target-exposure distribution q(j|u) from baseline sampler
        Compute training-only timestamp ages and category tau
        Compute a(u,j)=0.5+0.5*exp(-age(u,j)/tau)
        Compute Z_u=sum_j q(j|u)*a(u,j)
        If exposure law is unavailable: disable temporal arm
    For each baseline training update within fixed limits:
        Replay identical user/window and negative draws across objective controls
        features=Encode(sequence)
        Select identical valid input/positive positions in both objectives
        Sample up to 16 distinct eligible uniform negatives per position
        Exclude zero, target and observed training positives
        Skip positions with no eligible negative in both objectives
        Score positives and negatives using the same activation
        If baseline arm: compute documented baseline objective/reduction
        Else:
            log_mix=log_softmax(masked_negative_scores, dim=-1)
            loss=-logsumexp(log_mix+logsigmoid(positive_score[...,None]-negative_scores), dim=-1)
            Initially use negative-score penalty lambda=0
        If temporal arm: multiply each position loss by a(u,j)/Z_u
        Apply unchanged baseline per-window/user reduction; optimize
    Save one selected checkpoint with matching configuration beneath trial directory
Generate working/predict.py using identical encoding, scoring and category routing
Preserve diagnostic adapter interfaces and report measured metrics with definitions
Submit for unchanged host validation; compare only macro validation HR@10
Retain exactly one independently trained model per category without fusion

originality.positive: Combines explicit padding correctness with controlled competitive-negative ranking and target-exposure-normalized temporal supervision in the constrained GRU4Rec setting.
originality.negative: Packing, BPR-max, temporal decay and importance normalization are established; the contribution is a disciplined incremental adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Removes a directly measured encoding confound and establishes interpretable experiments on ranking discrimination and current-interest supervision.
future_potential.negative: No gains have been demonstrated, timestamp recency may suppress durable interests, and the method does not directly represent compatibility or satisfied needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses standard packed GRUs and a compact stable loss without additional independently trained components.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact exposure normalization, aligned scattering, deterministic replay, filtered negative sampling and checkpoint–predictor consistency require substantial integration and verification.

related_work.title: PyTorch packed recurrent sequences
contributions: Provides recurrent execution over valid variable-length prefixes.
Supports padding-invariant encoding after chronological compaction of left-padded histories.
With automatic sorting, unpacked outputs and returned hidden states are restored to input batch order.
limitations: Packing original left-padded tensors using nonzero counts processes incorrect positions.
Aligned timestep training and diagnostics require unpacking and scattering valid outputs.
Empty histories require explicit handling outside packed execution.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces BPR-max aggregation emphasizing high-scoring negatives.
Separates ranking probability aggregation from negative-score regularization.
limitations: Does not establish gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.
High-scoring unobserved items can be relevant false negatives.
The proposed history-filtered, distinct negative pools differ from official sampling.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec PyTorch implementation
contributions: Specifies BPR-max score activation, differentiable softmax weighting and the separate bpreg penalty.
Documents shared additional negative draws, popularity-powered sampling and batch-size loss reduction.
limitations: Official with-replacement sampling permits duplicates and does not apply the proposed complete training-history exclusion.
An adapted implementation must document changes to sampling, masking and reduction rather than claim exact reproduction.

related_work.title: PyTorch unpacking of packed sequences
contributions: Provides unpacking with total_length for stable aligned output dimensions.
Supports recovering chronological valid outputs before scattering to left-padded coordinates.
limitations: Unpacking alone does not restore original left-padding coordinates.
Correct recurrent outputs can still be misread through incorrect final-position indexing.

related_work.title: MTAM: time-aware attentive recurrent recommendation
contributions: Provides precedent for incorporating temporal information into recurrent recommendation.
Motivates studying recent behavior alongside historical memory.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed normalized user-relative target weighting.
Its broader temporal architecture adds complexity beyond the selected early-stage experiment.
